# Operator Note: Airborne Dust from Blasting (see SB-1014)

This note highlights key actions for operators following the safety bulletin on airborne dust generated by blasting. Airborne particulate from blasting can carry metal, oxides, and abrasive media that pose inhalation and eye hazards and can contaminate adjacent processes.

Actions for operators
- Review SB-1014 before performing or supporting blasting work. Confirm you understand the required controls and sign-off process where applicable.
- Use designated containment and local exhaust systems while blasting. Ensure curtains and enclosures are secured and free of gaps before starting operations.
- Wear the prescribed respiratory protection and eye protection. Inspect PPE for damage and proper fit prior to each use. Replace or decontaminate PPE per established procedures.
- Maintain housekeeping: use approved vacuum systems with high-efficiency filtration for cleanup. Do not use compressed air for dry sweeping or cleaning exposed surfaces.
- Coordinate with adjacent area operators to minimize cross-contamination. Close or seal process openings and remove or cover sensitive tooling and products.
- Report visible dust migration, damaged containment, or malfunctioning ventilation immediately to supervision. Stop work if controls are inadequate and await corrective action.
- Attend refresher training and participate in any monitoring or medical surveillance programs linked to blasting operations.

Follow SB-1014 for full details, reporting steps, and escalation paths. Safety first: stop and check if conditions change.
